dataSetInformation.common:generalComment: Dataset developed within the ARCADIA Project (production chain study regarding glass products for windows “PRODUZIONE DI LASTRE E SISTEMI IN VETRO PER INFISSI E SERRAMENTI”). The dataset refers to the production of float glass pane, representative of the Italian average processing technologies commonly used for glass production. The data set covers relevant process steps / technologies over the supply chain of the represented cradle to gate inventory with a good overall data quality. The inventory is based on primary data for the Float glass production, and on secondary data (literature and/or LCI datasets) representative of Italian supply chain. Float glass is used in windows for the building sector or in further processing and assembling. Dimensions: surface 1 m2, thickness 4 mm.

referenceToExternalDocumentation.common:shortDescription: Dalla Valle A., Lavagna M., Campioli A., 2023. “PRODUZIONE DI LASTRE E SISTEMI IN VETRO PER INFISSI E SERRAMENTI”. Internal report ARCADIA Project. Primary data of the main production processes (foreground data) collected from representative producers. Background dataset from Ecoinvent database cut-off (v. 3.6) were used for the LCA study.

locationOfOperationSupplyOrProduction.descriptionOfRestrictions: Italy. Primary data collected from leading glass producers active on national context. Dataset representative of Italian production of float glass pane.

technology.technologyDescriptionAndIncludedProcesse: Float glass is a clear, flat soda lime silicate glass with parallel surfaces. The production process begins with the transport and mixing of raw materials (silica sand, soda ash, dolomite, etc.) and their melting in a furnace. The molten glass is fed into a bath of molten tin, where serrated wheels pull and push the glass sideways depending on the desired thickness. The resulting float glass passes through a controlled cooling tunnel, exiting the lehr at room temperature. The glass is then cut lengthwise and crosswise, performing automatic inspections on regular samples to check the quality of the glass at each step in the glassmaking process. The sheets of float glass are finally packed and stored in the warehouse. Waste treatment and their transport to facilities is included and reflect the Italian waste treatments routes. The system boundary considers A1 “procurement of raw materials”, A2 “transport”, A3 “production”, according to EN15804:2012+A1:2013 standard. The Cradle-to-gate analysis includes the input of materials, energy, water and the outputs of waste, emissions and transport related to the considered system boundary. Equipment and infrastructures are not included in the foreground but accounted for in the background system. Primary data (from leading glass producers) and secondary data (from established database) representative of Italian supply chain for the geographical characteristics and technologies used were collected. Inventory data have been collected as physical quantities of resources (materials and energy) used in the different processes. The benefits from the production and use of energy from incineration and landfill were excluded, as well as those deriving from the use of secondary materials produced from recycling of waste materials. Background data were modelled according to Ecoinvent v.3.6.
technology.technologicalApplicability: Float glass is used as product applied into windows of building sector. Float glass is also intended for further processing (e.g. coating, lamination) and assemblies (e.g. insulated glass unit). Final product is applied into windows of building sector.

dataSourcesTreatmentAndRepresentativenes.dataCutOffAndCompletenessPrinciples: Production of equipment and infrastructures is not included, except for the background system.
dataSourcesTreatmentAndRepresentativenes.deviationsFromCutOffAndCompletenessPrinc: None for the inventory. Completeness related to elementary flows cannot be evaluated.

review.common:reviewDetails: The review was performed in compliance with Arcadia Metodology “Metodologia per gli studi di filiera della Banca Dati italiana LCA” and ISO 14040-44. The dataset has been assessed limited to the foreground data collected during the supply chain studies. Each dataset has been evaluated on the basis of the following 4 criteria: 1. Technological Representative; 2. Time Representative; 3. Geographic Representative; 4. Reliability. In this context the Reliability is very good. The data used are consistent, appropriate and reasonable in view of the goal and scope of the study. The system boundaries include all relevant processes and activity types from cradle to gate. A cut-off has been applied to production of equipment and infrastructure and to the processes involved in the recycling of glass. These are in line with the requirements of the “Metodologia per gli studi di filiera della Banca Dati italiana LCA” (Buttol et al., v2, November 2021). The LCI modelling choices follow the requirements of Buttol et al. (2021), such as allocation, consistency of included processes, and LCI methodology in general. It has been consistently applied along the whole dataset. The representativeness of the dataset (time-related, geographical, technology) is well documented and very good, thanks also to the involvement of relevant market operators. The precision and completeness of the dataset cannot be evaluated.
review.common:otherReviewDetails: The study was judged by the reviewer as compliant with both ISO 14040-44 and Arcadia methodology.
